title: Merge the shelves
scenario: Two shelves are sorted smallest to biggest. Merge them into one sorted shelf.

intro.job: Two shelves are sorted smallest to biggest. Merge them into one sorted shelf.

idea.rule: The leftovers still count — when one list runs out, append the rest of the other.
idea.detail: Two fingers, one at the front of each shelf. Compare the two items they point at, move the smaller one to the new shelf, and step that finger forward. When one shelf runs out the comparing is over — but the other shelf may still have items, already in order, that belong on the end.

watch.code:
a, b = pair
out = []
i = 0
j = 0
while i < len(a) and j < len(b):
    if a[i] <= b[j]:
        out.append(a[i])
        i += 1
    else:
        out.append(b[j])
        j += 1
out = out + a[i:] + b[j:]
print(out)

model_restatement: Combine the two sorted lists into one sorted list, keeping every item.

clarify.question: What if both shelves have the same number?
clarify.answer: Keep both — either order is fine.

clarify.question: Could a shelf be empty?
clarify.answer: Not today — each has at least one item.

clarify.question: Can I just sort everything?
clarify.answer: That works — but here, use the order that's already there.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Walk both shelves with two fingers. While both have items, move the smaller one to the new shelf. Print the new shelf.

why_line: The loop stops the moment the first shelf runs out (i reaches 3) — the 6 is still waiting on the second shelf, and nothing after the loop picks it up.

explain.rule: Stopping when one shelf is empty is closing up shop while customers are still in line — whatever's left on the other shelf never gets served.
explain.bridge: When the loop ends, which shelf still has items — and where do they go?

fix.rule: After the loop, out + a[i:] + b[j:] tacks on whatever's left — one of the two slices is empty, the other is already sorted.

walk.gloss: While both shelves still have items...
Move it to the new shelf, and step that finger forward.
One shelf ran out — add the rest of the other, already in order.
